cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a hand-woven indigo strip-cloth gown (riga/tobe/boubou style) with embroidered neckline and pocket, a traditional West African men's garment made from narrow hand-loomed strips — a form used by Wolof and neighboring West African groups, consistent with the claim.

physical.title: gown; textile; tobe
physical.summary: Man’s gown (boubou, tobe, riga), hand-woven from hand-spun cotton dyed indigo. The body is formed of 141 narrow strips hand-sewn together along the selvedges vertically, while the sleeves are sewn horizontally. The body of the gown is rectangular in shape, while the sleeves flare out being wider at the top than at the bottom. At the front is sewn a square pocket. The gown is hand-embroidered in a different blue cotton thread in the ‘two knives’ (aska biyu) pattern around the neck and pocket. There are small spirals on the front and back of the garment. There is a hand-sewn hem around the neck and sleeves.
